people.name: Zohran Mamdani
facts: Born in Kampala, Uganda, and moved to New York City as a child.
Represented Queens in the New York State Assembly from 2021.
Elected mayor of New York City in 2025, the city’s first Muslim mayor.

people.name: Salah al-Din
facts: Kurdish-born founder of the Ayyubid dynasty, he ruled Egypt and Syria in the 12th century.
Recaptured Jerusalem from the Crusaders in 1187.
Respected even by his enemies for his mercy and chivalry.

people.name: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq
facts: The closest companion of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and the first adult man to accept Islam.
Travelled with the Prophet on the Hijrah from Makkah to Madinah.
Became the first caliph after the Prophet passed away in 632 and led the Muslim community for about two years.

people.name: Omar Suleiman
facts: American imam and scholar from New Orleans.
Founder and president of the Yaqeen Institute for Islamic Research.
Known for his lectures and his civil rights and interfaith work.

people.name: Khadijah bint Khuwaylid
facts: A successful merchant in Makkah who hired Muhammad ﷺ to lead her trade caravans.
Married the Prophet and was the first person to accept Islam.
Supported him with her wealth and comfort through the hardest early years of his mission.

people.name: Khawla bint al-Azwar
facts: A 7th-century Arab Muslim warrior.
Fought in the early Muslim campaigns in the Levant, including the Battle of Yarmouk in 636.
Remembered for riding into battle to rescue her brother Dirar.

people.name: Abdul El-Sayed
facts: American doctor and epidemiologist from Michigan who taught at Columbia University.
Led Detroit’s health department from 2015, rebuilding it after the city’s bankruptcy.
Ran for governor of Michigan in 2018.

people.name: Greta Thunberg
facts: Swedish activist who started skipping school on Fridays in 2018 to protest outside parliament for climate action.
Her “school strike for climate” grew into the worldwide Fridays for Future movement.
Spoke to world leaders at the UN Climate Action Summit in 2019.

people.name: Imam al-Bukhari
facts: A 9th-century scholar born in 810 in Bukhara, in today’s Uzbekistan.
Spent years travelling to collect and check the sayings of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
His collection, Sahih al-Bukhari, is regarded by Sunni Muslims as the most authentic book after the Quran.

people.name: Ilhan Omar
facts: Came to the United States as a refugee from Somalia when she was a child.
In 2019 she became one of the first two Muslim women elected to the US Congress, representing Minnesota.
The first member of Congress to wear a hijab on the House floor.

people.name: Abraham Lincoln
facts: Grew up on the American frontier and was mostly self-taught.
Led the United States through the Civil War.
Issued the Emancipation Proclamation in 1863 and pushed for the amendment that abolished slavery.

people.name: Mahatma Gandhi
facts: Indian lawyer who led India’s struggle for independence from British rule.
Championed non-violent resistance, such as the 1930 Salt March.
Inspired civil rights movements around the world, including Martin Luther King Jr.

people.name: Martin Luther King Jr.
facts: American Baptist minister who led the civil rights movement in the 1950s and 1960s.
Gave the “I Have a Dream” speech at the 1963 March on Washington.
Won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1964.

people.name: Malcolm X
facts: American minister and one of the most influential voices of the civil rights era.
After performing Hajj in 1964, he embraced Sunni Islam and took the name el-Hajj Malik el-Shabazz.
His life story, The Autobiography of Malcolm X, is still widely read.

people.name: Amira Elghawaby
facts: Canadian journalist and human rights advocate.
In 2023 she became Canada’s first Special Representative on Combatting Islamophobia.
Previously worked with the National Council of Canadian Muslims.

people.name: Nelson Mandela
facts: South African leader who fought against apartheid and spent 27 years in prison.
Became South Africa’s first Black president in 1994.
Shared the Nobel Peace Prize in 1993.

people.name: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ
facts: Born in Makkah around the year 570.
Received the first revelation of the Quran at age 40 in the cave of Hira.
Known even before prophethood as al-Amin, “the trustworthy”.

people.name: Prophet Musa (AS)
facts: The prophet mentioned by name most often in the Quran.
Raised in Pharaoh’s palace in Egypt, he later led the Children of Israel out of slavery.
Received the Tawrah (Torah) and spoke directly with God.
